## Overview Keep DeepSeek-V4 mHC and FP8 output-projection arithmetic stable across token batch positions. BI mode uses explicit mHC pre/post stages with a split choice equivalent to one token; default execution retains fused mHC. Hopper's non-TMA FP8 scale path uses per-group Triton block-scaled matmul. Blackwell keeps TMA-packed UE8M0 scales on DeepGEMM `fp8_einsum` without reshaping them into an invalid layout. The first-layer mHC broadcast is refreshed in place after weight reload. ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Token hidden states"] --> B["mHC pre
fixed BI split"] --> C["Attention / FFN"] --> D["mHC post
fixed BI split"] --> E["Token output"] F["FP8 o-proj scales"] --> G["Hopper: Triton
Blackwell: DeepGEMM"] --> C classDef io fill:#e7f1ee,stroke:#2c9d86,stroke-width:1.5px,stroke-dasharray:5 4,color:#263d36; classDef module fill:#d5e2de,stroke:#abc8bf,color:#263d36; classDef core fill:#0a6953,stroke:#0a6953,color:#ffffff; class A,E,F io; class B,D,G module; class C core; linkStyle default stroke:#6b817a,stroke-width:1.5px; ``` ## Test Local lint, compile, and diff checks passed. On H20, the standalone mHC anchor-token exact-equality regression and the existing DeepSeek-V4 weight-finalization hook test each passed. An isolated o-proj benchmark was not run. ### Acc H100 DP4/EP4, four-layer, two-step integration with the other DeepSeek-V4 changes and weight reload: `training/rollout_probs_diff_valid=1`, maximum/mean difference **0**, and KL **0** at both steps (`max_num_batched_tokens=1024`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.55`). The 2048-token setting OOMed on this 80 GB setup. This is a combined-path result, not an isolated P4 evaluation. ## H20 integrated end-to-end validation (2026-11-03) This supplement supersedes earlier single-GPU OOM or missing-server attempts **for the integrated DeepSeek-V4 stack only**. It does not claim that this individual PR head alone passes the full-model run. The tested integration commit is `5931b43d3287c1486fb319d1e5687cbe43c8bf00`, combining the V4 split PRs, follow-up integration fixes and the H20 FlashInfer top-k fallback in [inaniloquentee/vllm#6](https://github.com/inaniloquentee/vllm/pull/6). Code and raw logs are confined to `/home/ljj`; no repository test file was added for this validation. H20-3e, TP8, model `/home/ljj/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base`, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1`, `VLLM_DS4_DECODE_KERNEL=sparse`, `VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`. Same model/configuration on upstream main `7651825993d001759107c66cdf6983535900c874` (raw `/home/ljj/vllm-dsv4-main-baseline-20261103/fullmodel-tp-eager-main-2.log`): ```text ValueError: FP8 MoE backend DEEPGEMM does not support the deployment configuration since kernel does not support batch invariance. ``` Main cannot reach a same-BI `lm_eval` or serving benchmark, so there is no comparable main throughput claim. An intermediate integrated stack `71f3d9aa9` with SM100-only DeepSelect on H20 also failed graph capture (raw `/home/ljj/vllm-dsv4-e2e-20261103/e2e-service/server.log`): ```text CUDA error (/workspace/.deps/deepselect-src/csrc/cuda_kernels/v3_fp32/instantiations/../topk_select.cuh:590): no kernel image is available for execution on the device ``` After integrating the H20 dispatch, the exact full-model command runs under the same Slurm eight-GPU allocation. The external test script is `/home/ljj/tmp/run-dsv4-fullmodel-e2e-20261103.sh`; it checks token IDs, generated logprobs and prompt logprobs for 128/512/2048 tokens in three batch positions: ```bash srun --partition=h20 --nodelist=vllm-sgp-h20-03 --gres=gpu:8 --cpus-per-task=64 --mem=512G --time=03:00:00 --export=ALL,REPO=/home/ljj/vllm-dsv4-e2e-20261103,MODEL=/home/ljj/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base,RESULT=/home/ljj/tmp/dsv4-e2e-zero-diff-5931b43d3.json,VLLM_DS4_DECODE_KERNEL=sparse bash /home/ljj/tmp/run-dsv4-fullmodel-e2e-20261103.sh # Repeat with DSV4_E2E_GRAPH=1, DSV4_E2E_EP=1, and both set to 1. ``` Raw final line in each of `/home/ljj/vllm-dsv4-e2e-20261103/fullmodel-tp-eager-7.log`, `fullmodel-tp-graph-5931.log`, `fullmodel-ep-eager-5931.log`, `fullmodel-ep-graph-5931.log`: ```text PASS: 9 full-model exact comparisons PASS: 9 full-model exact comparisons PASS: 9 full-model exact comparisons PASS: 9 full-model exact comparisons ``` Serve the same commit with: ```bash vllm serve /home/ljj/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base --tensor-parallel-size 8 --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.82 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9256 vllm bench serve --model /home/ljj/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base --dataset-name random --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9256 --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1 --request-rate inf --num-prompts 128 --num-warmups 16 lm-eval run --model local-completions --model_args base_url=http://127.0.0.1:9256/v1/completions,model=/home/ljj/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base,num_concurrent=64 --tasks gsm8k --trust_remote_code ``` Raw `/home/ljj/vllm-dsv4-e2e-20261103/e2e-service-flashinfer/bench-serve.log`: ```text ============ Serving Benchmark Result ============ Successful requests: 128 Failed requests: 0 Benchmark duration (s): 120.00 Total input tokens: 1048576 Total generated tokens: 128 Request throughput (req/s): 1.07 Output token throughput (tok/s): 1.07 Total token throughput (tok/s): 8738.89 ``` Raw `/home/ljj/vllm-dsv4-e2e-20261103/e2e-service-flashinfer/lm-eval-gsm8k.log` (all 1319 questions, five-shot): ```text |Tasks|Version| Filter |n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| |-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9234|± |0.0073| | | |strict-match | 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9234|± |0.0073| ``` No AI-generated performance table: the blocks above are excerpts of the raw logs. The integration SHA and full log paths are provided so the evidence can be audited on the shared H20 devbox. ## Latest-main H20 validation (2026-11-03) Head `58f67e17ccbd61d65d83d7161bc80e03d965fa7f` merges upstream main `3d18166d453aa8ae73fbc2327c35f0827db55416`. The conflict in `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer.forward` was resolved by retaining main's `reuse_residual` argument for the fused path and the V4 BI unfused post/pre path when `use_fused_mhc` is false. No new test file. `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` had no output; GitHub now reports this PR mergeable. Existing mHC BI test on H20-3e (one allocated GPU): ```bash srun --partition=h20 --gres=gpu:1 --time=00:30:00 --chdir=/home/ljj/vllm-pr59929-main-20261103 --output=/home/ljj/vllm-pr59929-main-20261103/mhc-focused-flashmla-sm90.log /usr/bin/env PATH=/home/ljj/vllm-pr-59863/.venv/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/local/cuda/bin:/usr/bin:/bin LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/home/ljj/toolchains/gcc13/lib:/usr/local/cuda-13.0/lib64 PYTHONPATH=/home/ljj/vllm-pr59929-main-20261103 /home/ljj/vllm-pr-59863/.venv/bin/pytest -q -rs tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py -k mhc_pre_batch_invariance --tb=short ``` Raw `/home/ljj/vllm-pr59929-main-20261103/mhc-focused-flashmla-sm90.log`: ```text 1 passed, 348 deselected, 3 warnings in 17.07s ``` The fresh `/home/ljj` worktree reused existing local `_vllm_fa2_C`, `_vllm_fa3_C`, `_C_stable_libtorch` binaries and `flash_mla_interface.py` through symlinks, all pointing inside `/home/ljj`; the first two collection attempts without those build artifacts failed with missing import errors (`mhc-focused-sm90.log`, `mhc-focused-built-ext-sm90.log`). This is a focused kernel test only. Full-model `lm_eval` and `vllm bench serve` have **not** been rerun on this exact rebased PR head; prior integrated results in this body belong to their documented integration SHA. DCO and the pre-run label gate still require human action before merge. ## Contribution and review AI-assisted update. This PR owns model mHC/o-proj alignment; it does not reimplement the FP8 quantizer (#59863), sparse top-k/decode (#60442-#60454), MoE/DeepEP (#59925), or split-K matmul (#59952). Additional motivation from GLM-5.3 Flash on GB10/SM121: we independently traced batch-layout differences to the same two mHC choices addressed here. Posting this on the existing PR rather than opening a duplicate report.

Our historical fixture uses GLM layer-0/layer-3 mHC parameters, synthetic seeded BF16 inputs, hidden size 4096 and hc multiplier 4. It moves identical anchor rows among batches of 1, 8, 16, 23, 258, 516, 522, 774, 1293, 1548, 1550 and 2048 rows. Fixed-shape repeats are exact.

- Native dispatch: 38 failed component batch-invariance cases.
- Fixed prenorm split count only: 22 failures remain.
- Fixed split count plus a consistent separate post/pre composition: zero failures in this fixture.

The remaining differences after fixing splits came from switching between the small-row fused arithmetic and the larger-row composition. This matters for comparing speculative drafters because proposal/admission changes alter target verification layouts even with shared token histories.

This is historical component evidence, not a test of this PR or a full-model quality claim. Source SHA256 pins for that fixture are `c8ce81539c779436eb2b9fbba84738f3114bf3ac0a149f2b606f7d38bd1067ce` (`tilelang.py`) and `03aeb3f7c0eabfe8391006ff80f8d4cfedba7cf3d0a168e0dee2d678d3e3bd24` (`tilelang_kernels.py`). A consistent policy also changes some default C1 rounding, so we keep its full-model quality and serving-overhead checks separate.

The shared-helper changes here are relevant to GLM too; GLM's model call sites should also be checked for the consistent post/pre path as this work lands. We have not yet qualified GLM against this PR. Related MoE verification evidence is on #46639: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46639#issuecomment-6318857951.

@@ -1019,6 +1019,67 @@ def _torch_hc_prenorm_gemm(
     sqrsum[0].copy_(x_float.square().sum(dim=-1))
 
 
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not HAS_TILELANG_MHC,
+    reason="TileLang MHC support required",
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("hidden_size", [4096])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("hc_mult", [4])
+def test_mhc_pre_batch_invariance(monkeypatch, hidden_size, hc_mult):
+    """One token's output must be bitwise independent of the batch it runs in."""
+    import vllm.envs as envs
+
+    monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT", "1")
+    monkeypatch.setattr(envs, "VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT", True)
+    torch.set_default_device(DEVICE)
+    set_random_seed(0)
+
+    pool = 2048
+    hc_mult2 = hc_mult * hc_mult
+    hc_mult3 = 2 * hc_mult + hc_mult2
+    residual_pool = torch.randn((pool, hc_mult, hidden_size), dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    fn = (
+        torch.randn((hc_mult3, hc_mult, hidden_size), dtype=torch.float)
+        * 1e-4
+        * (1 + torch.arange(hc_mult).mul(0.01).view(1, -1, 1))
+    ).flatten(1, 2)
+    hc_scale = torch.randn((3,), dtype=torch.float) * 0.1
+    hc_base = torch.randn((hc_mult3,), dtype=torch.float) * 0.1
+    norm_weight = torch.ones((hidden_size,), dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+
+    hc_sinkhorn_eps = hc_pre_eps = rms_eps = norm_eps = 1e-6
+    sinkhorn_repeat = 20
+    hc_post_alpha = 1.0
+
+    def run(residual):
+        return torch.ops.vllm.mhc_pre_tilelang(
+            residual,
+            fn,
+            hc_scale,
+            hc_base,
+            rms_eps,
+            hc_pre_eps,
+            hc_sinkhorn_eps,
+            hc_post_alpha,
+            sinkhorn_repeat,
+            1,
+            norm_weight,
+            norm_eps,
+        )
+
+    anchor = residual_pool[0:1].clone()
+    ref = run(anchor)
+
+    for num_tokens in (1, 2, 7, 63, 64, 65, 127, 128, 129, 511, 512, 1000):
+        filler = residual_pool[1:num_tokens]
+        for pos in sorted({0, num_tokens // 2, num_tokens - 1}):
+            batch = torch.cat([filler[:pos], anchor, filler[pos:]], dim=0)
+            assert batch.shape[0] == num_tokens
+            for actual, expected in zip(run(batch), ref, strict=True):
+                assert torch.equal(actual[pos : pos + 1], expected), (
+                    f"batch invariance broken: num_tokens={num_tokens} pos={pos}"
+                )
+

     reason="TileLang MHC support required",

🚀

Additional motivation from GLM-5.3 Flash on GB10/SM121: we independently traced batch-layout differences to the same two mHC choices addressed here. Posting this on the existing PR rather than opening a duplicate report.

Our historical fixture uses GLM layer-0/layer-3 mHC parameters, synthetic seeded BF16 inputs, hidden size 4096 and hc multiplier 4. It moves identical anchor rows among batches of 1, 8, 16, 23, 258, 516, 522, 774, 1293, 1548, 1550 and 2048 rows. Fixed-shape repeats are exact.

- Native dispatch: 38 failed component batch-invariance cases.
- Fixed prenorm split count only: 22 failures remain.
- Fixed split count plus a consistent separate post/pre composition: zero failures in this fixture.

The remaining differences after fixing splits came from switching between the small-row fused arithmetic and the larger-row composition. This matters for comparing speculative drafters because proposal/admission changes alter target verification layouts even with shared token histories.

This is historical component evidence, not a test of this PR or a full-model quality claim. Source SHA256 pins for that fixture are `c8ce81539c779436eb2b9fbba84738f3114bf3ac0a149f2b606f7d38bd1067ce` (`tilelang.py`) and `03aeb3f7c0eabfe8391006ff80f8d4cfedba7cf3d0a168e0dee2d678d3e3bd24` (`tilelang_kernels.py`). A consistent policy also changes some default C1 rounding, so we keep its full-model quality and serving-overhead checks separate.

The shared-helper changes here are relevant to GLM too; GLM's model call sites should also be checked for the consistent post/pre path as this work lands. We have not yet qualified GLM against this PR. Related MoE verification evidence is on #46639: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46639#issuecomment-6318857951.
